title: Doodlume — distinctive playable design system
disclosure: Simulated perspectives inspired by public work. The named people did not participate, and these comments are not their quotations or endorsements.
brief:
# Doodlume visual system review
Owner explicitly authorizes critical design research, design system and homepage/studio implementation. No video/deadline work. Distinctive, calm, expressive, premium creative gaming product; not generic SaaS/LLM landing page. Desktop primary. No all-black app, no sage/cream reversion, no noisy decorative motion or excess copy. Preserve functional create/draw/upload, play/edit/save/reopen, game controls and original art. No fabricated 10 ratings, no actual external endorsement.

Scope: entire homepage (header/hero/live examples/how-it-works/closing/footer), studio entry, create dialog, play frame and controls; loading/error/accessibility states via code and browser. Not model quality or deeper gameplay redesign in this visual phase.

E1: current full homepage inspected live top-to-bottom 1440x900 at localhost5192; before screenshots output/playwright/home-audit-1440.png and cat-home-fixed-1440.png. Source src/components/Home.tsx, Home.css. Conventional equal-level two-column hero, small examples selector, much whitespace and abstract duplicated bottom text. Primary create links and real playable examples work. Preserve original art identity and truthful example labels.
E2: studio fresh session inspected live: #studio. Header My worlds, New world/settings. Creation band Your image. Your game. Draw/upload. Default Wandering Grove play frame + toolbar. Existing typography Manrope everywhere and many hardcoded cobalt shades. src/App.tsx, src/styles.css, src/studio.css. Fresh studio currently shows a different older example than the homepage. Need coherent transition without deleting gameplay.
E3: create dialog inspected live: upload/draw/phone, source type selector, optional idea, collapsed gameplay details, disabled Create before image. Existing dialogs and behavior must survive. src/components/CreateWorldModal.tsx or locate actual component via rg. Don't invent behavior.
E4: public reference research: https://play.date/ (distinctive product identity and inviting games), https://lusion.co/ (immersive interactive storytelling), https://www.figma.com/ (creative tool interaction), https://spline.design/ (creation and interactive product proof). These are lenses, not objectively best or permission to copy layouts/assets. Research source text inspected by root; no third party metrics claimed.
E5: technical constraints: existing React/Phaser lazy loaded game, local source artwork. No new WebGL marketing renderer, framework migration, autoplay audio or paid generation needed. Need semantic controls, motion reduction, stable loading frame, 1280x720/1440x900/1920x1080 inspection, keyboard focus and scoped contrast checks. Saved game artifacts must stay intact.

Read assigned seat from /Users/sreenath/.codex/skills/product-council/references/roster.md and JSON contract references/data-contract.md. Return actual authored review as JSON file outputs/design-reset/reviews/R{round}-{seat}.json. Approximately150–250words where useful, one round1proposal each, later no need newproposals. References E1–E5 valid. Every laterround responds to another seat from prior complete rounds. No browser tooling concurrent with root; inspect source and supplied screenshot files with view_image. No product edits. Root will collect complete earlier rounds in outputs/design-reset/council.json before next round.
execution: Ten independent simulated reviewer agents, three active at a time; four rounds sharing complete preceding rounds. Root inspects browser and source and implements authorized changes. No actual named experts participated.

contributions.assessment: The premium direction should make the real artwork and playable proof more prominent while retaining the existing on-demand game boundary. Home.tsx defers WorldCanvas and SketchPad; that is valuable architecture, not a visual compromise. The initial example picker, however, uses each full source image as a tiny thumbnail, so deferred JavaScript alone does not establish a lightweight first visit.
strengths: The game mounts after deliberate Play; source art supplies useful proof before gameplay initializes.
The stage has a reserved aspect ratio, explicit pending text, fetch cancellation, and retry UI. Source inspection shows intent to preserve focus during loading.
concerns: The three picker images reuse full source assets without thumbnail variants. Local disk sizes are approximately 2.3 MB for rover and 1.7 MB for cat; these are file observations, not measured browser transfer totals.
Fetch completion sets playing before the lazy renderer is ready; the visual reset must cover the complete transition through the first usable game frame, not only the JSON request.

proposals.action: Establish a measured homepage performance guardrail: preserve click-to-load gameplay, provide dedicated picker thumbnails, reserve the play frame through loading and failure, and use CSS for brand expression without another WebGL renderer.
proposals.rationale: An expressive page can become more convincing without charging every visitor for inactive artwork or decorative runtime work.
proposals.validation: Record cold-cache initial transfer, JavaScript cost, layout shifts, and Play-to-ready timing before and after. Proposed budgets: zero game-runtime requests before Play, picker thumbnails at most 30 KB each, and no frame-size change between pending and ready states. Test throttled loading and failed requests; report actual results separately from targets.

contributions.position: Preserve the lazy game architecture and spend the visual budget on composition, type, and existing artwork.
contributions.uncertainty: No network waterfall, timing profile, or field performance data was measured in this independent review. Source and the supplied desktop screenshot cannot prove responsiveness under load.

contributions.assessment: The visual hierarchy can change substantially without replacing the working creation and game lifecycle. Home already owns its example session, while App owns draft, dialog, library and gameplay state. Treat those boundaries as a preservation constraint, not an excuse to preserve the conventional two-column composition.
strengths: Home defers the game and sketch renderer until needed and already preserves play state when drawing an invention.
Studio cancels background interpretation when inactive, retains source and idea, and gates play behind dialogs; these are valuable interaction contracts.
concerns: A redesigned stage that moves or conditionally duplicates WorldCanvas could silently restart play, lose keyboard focus or detach contextual controls.

App contains substantial state and creation markup; a visual pass coupled to broad state extraction would make regressions harder to isolate. The older fresh-studio example also weakens continuity with the homepage.

proposals.action: Recompose the homepage around one persistent playable stage and restyle the studio with small presentational shells for its entry, controls and dialog surfaces. Keep existing session ownership, creation handlers, storage schema and canvas lifecycle intact; audit intentional example changes separately.
proposals.rationale: This permits a distinctive visual structure while preserving draw/upload, play, edit, save and reopen. Share visual tokens and control primitives only where semantics match.
proposals.validation: Exercise draw and upload entry, pause/resume, invention editing, source viewing, save/reopen and homepage/studio return; verify no unexpected canvas remount or lost draft and no stale dialog after navigation.

contributions.position: Support structural visual redesign with a narrow implementation boundary around existing behavior; do not introduce a framework migration or generalized state rewrite.
contributions.uncertainty: Source and supplied desktop screenshot inspected; this seat has not independently exercised browser interactions or measured canvas remounts.

contributions.assessment: The browser behavior already provides a better foundation than the conventional marketing composition suggests. The real artwork becomes a playable surface after an explicit action; that transformation should be the visual centerpiece. Premium character can come from composition and precise state changes without an additional animation runtime.
strengths: Home.tsx uses real anchors for navigation and buttons for example selection, defers WorldCanvas, cancels obsolete fetches, and guards keyboard focus when the visitor moves away during loading.
Modal.tsx uses the native dialog top layer and restores focus across nested tools. Preserve these capabilities through the visual reset.
concerns: At normal desktop heights the example frame follows different source aspect ratios, so switching examples can move the surrounding controls; the short-screen CSS already recognizes the value of a stable frame.
The studio opens a different example from the homepage. Even a strong visual redesign will feel discontinuous if the artifact and interaction vocabulary change at entry.

proposals.action: Build the new visual centerpiece around a stable artwork stage and a persistent labeled control rail; use restrained CSS feedback for hover, pressed, loading and selected states, retaining explicit Play and the existing dialog/focus behavior.
proposals.rationale: Visitors should experience their illustration becoming interactive while navigation and controls remain predictable. This supports expressive visual identity without decorative motion or new rendering infrastructure.
proposals.validation: Check all three examples at 1280×720, 1440×900 and 1920×1080; verify source/play/pause/error transitions, keyboard focus after delayed loading, dialog return focus, and reduced-motion behavior. Record visual movement rather than assuming stability.

contributions.position: Favor a more distinctive composition while preserving the existing browser-native interaction foundation; no framework migration or scroll-driven spectacle.
contributions.uncertainty: I inspected Home source/CSS, Modal source and the supplied desktop screenshot. Browser interaction outcomes and measured layout movement remain unverified by this seat.

contributions.assessment: The strongest foundation is behavioral: Home uses real links and buttons, explicit pressed states, and a deliberate keyboard handoff into the playable canvas. The native Modal already manages dismissal and return focus. An expressive visual reset should build on those contracts. The screenshots show a readable main message, but controls and explanatory labels feel subordinate to the artwork; their 9–12px CSS sizes deserve attention before adding ornamental detail.
strengths: Home.tsx preserves source artwork with object-fit: contain, hides the inactive game with inert, exposes moments through a polite live region, and avoids stealing focus after visitors move elsewhere.
Modal.tsx uses showModal, an associated heading, Escape dismissal, and explicit opener restoration; preserve this rather than replacing it with a visually styled generic overlay.
concerns: Home.css hardcodes a separate palette while studio.css provides semantic colors over a large legacy stylesheet. A new palette applied only to prominent surfaces can leave focus, disabled, error, and selected states visually disconnected.

The 28px minimum stage-action buttons and small instruction text offer little comfortable interaction space. Contrast cannot be certified from these screenshots; computed foreground/background pairs and focus visibility still need inspection.

proposals.action: Build the new visual vocabulary on semantic surface, ink, accent, focus, error, and selection tokens; enlarge essential stage controls and retain native dialog and game-focus behavior.
proposals.rationale: Brand expression and dependable interaction can share one system without rewriting working state management.
proposals.validation: Inspect all agreed desktop sizes plus 200% zoom; traverse create, close, play, pause, original, retry, and example selection by keyboard. Measure text and control contrast, check visible unclipped focus, reduced motion, and loading-frame stability.

contributions.position: Preserve semantic and focus behavior while changing the expressive shell; do not equate distinctive design with animated controls or finer text.
contributions.uncertainty: Source and two supplied desktop screenshots inspected; browser keyboard behavior, computed contrast, and zoom layouts remain unverified by this seat.

contributions.assessment: The visual reset needs a shared product language before it needs another homepage skin. Home.css owns hardcoded ink, accent, focus, border and radius values while studio.css already defines semantic color roles and then overrides legacy styles. This makes the journey feel assembled from separate releases. Preserve contextual differences: the homepage can be spacious and expressive while the studio remains compact and practical.
strengths: Original artwork supplies distinctive color without requiring decorative interface noise.
The studio already names useful roles for surfaces, stage chrome, disabled controls and errors; these provide a migration foothold.
concerns: The homepage primary action, selected example, focus ring and studio primary action use several unrelated cobalt values.
Repeated selector overrides and legacy color names make a new appended theme likely to leave dialogs and secondary states behind.

proposals.action: Establish one small semantic token layer and common action, field, selection and play-frame treatments; migrate existing homepage, studio and modal rules to it, removing superseded declarations. Allow explicit spacious and compact variants.
proposals.rationale: A shared accent, type hierarchy, edge treatment and interaction vocabulary can carry a distinctive identity through creation without forcing marketing and editing into the same layout.
proposals.validation: Compare homepage, studio and create dialog at all three requested desktop sizes; check normal, hover, focus, selected, disabled, loading and error states against the same role definitions. Confirm original art and all game controls remain usable.

contributions.position: Prioritize consolidation during the redesign, not as a later cleanup. Reuse visual behavior where meaning matches and keep layout differences purposeful.
contributions.uncertainty: I inspected the supplied homepage screenshot and stylesheet source; studio and modal visual findings rely partly on the brief's recorded inspection. Complete unused-rule removal needs a behavior inventory.

contributions.assessment: The interface is composed neatly but its hierarchy reads as a software landing template: a medium headline, adjacent rectangular demo, and subdued explanation rows. The art has personality; the surrounding typography and spacing do not yet amplify it.
strengths: The original rover illustration provides a strong focal point without decorative marketing assets.
The primary creation button is visually clear, and the live frame already groups caption, image and controls.
concerns: At 1440px the 58px hero top padding plus vertically centered text leaves its eyebrow far below the demo caption. This creates two unrelated reading starts.
The 9px showcase label, 10px eyebrows, 11px footer and 12px example names make useful context feel incidental; 44px thumbnails cannot communicate these very different worlds.
Manrope at every level, several near-identical cobalt values, and repeated 5–8px boxes produce uniformity without an identifiable visual grammar.

proposals.action: Build a bright gamefolio composition: an oversized compact display headline above a dominant playable plate, with a narrow creation rail and three clearly legible artwork tabs. Use pale violet-white surfaces, deep aubergine ink and one electric violet action color. Pair the existing Fraunces display face selectively with Manrope interface text; set 14px minimum meaningful labels, a 16/24 body rhythm, and an 8px spacing scale. Carry the same plate caption, action heights and typography into studio and creation dialogs.
proposals.rationale: A deliberate display/interface contrast and an art-first silhouette create distinction through structure rather than ornament.
proposals.validation: Compare complete pages at all three desktop sizes; creation and example entry must remain immediately visible at 1280×720, with untruncated labels and no game controls below a clipped frame.

contributions.position: Advocate a stronger change in composition and typographic roles, not merely new colors.
contributions.uncertainty: The 1440px screenshot and source substantiate hierarchy findings; alternate compositions still require browser validation, especially at short viewport heights.

contributions.assessment: The product has two legitimate first tasks: try a real game and make one from personal art. Both are available, but the journey changes vocabulary and action priority: homepage Make a game opens upload, studio emphasizes Draw here, and the dialog asks to Create a world. The visual reset should make these transitions feel like one task.
strengths: Playable examples establish the outcome before asking for an upload.
Optional idea and collapsed gameplay settings keep creation approachable; resume-draft behavior protects effort.
concerns: The fresh studio introduces a different example, creating an unnecessary comprehension reset.
Create world is disabled before an image, but the footer offers no adjacent explanation of the missing prerequisite.
Abstract closing copy does less to help someone begin than the explicit hero description.

proposals.action: Use a consistent Make a game action across home and studio, with clearly labeled Upload image and Draw here paths in the creation entry. Preserve direct drawing links and draft resumption. Explain the image prerequisite beside disabled creation; keep idea optional and gameplay collapsed. Replace closing ambiguity with the same concrete action. Label studio examples clearly and align the initial example with the homepage.
proposals.rationale: Stable labels and visible prerequisites reduce interpretation at each transition without adding steps or deleting working controls.
proposals.validation: At desktop widths, follow upload, drawing, close/resume, and saved-world reopening without losing state. At 390px verify basic reachable actions, readable labels, and no horizontal form overflow.

contributions.position: Prioritize continuity and task clarity before extra explanatory copy or onboarding.
contributions.uncertainty: Inspected the homepage screenshot and creation source; no measured completion or abandonment data. Mobile recommendations are basic usability checks, not a gameplay redesign.

contributions.assessment: The core promise is understandable, but the experience divides attention between making and sampling before explaining their relationship. Premium identity should come from the visible transformation of personal art into purposeful play, not a luxury styling layer.
strengths: The real, controllable examples provide stronger product evidence than a rendered mockup.
Drawing your own rescue part makes the creative promise tangible; original-art comparison can establish continuity.
concerns: The largest artwork and its Play action can make the page read as a game catalogue while Make a game begins an upload flow elsewhere.
The studio's different default example interrupts the narrative and can leave a newcomer unsure whether this is their work.
The closing question repeats aspiration without clarifying the next concrete action; the source-art disclosure appears only after opening the original.

proposals.action: Build one coherent invitation: label the interactive stage as a sample, show its source-to-play relationship with truthful source provenance, keep Make your game as the primary action, and make fresh studio entry visibly distinguish the sample from the visitor's creations. Replace abstract closing copy with a concrete draw/upload invitation.
proposals.rationale: Visitors should understand what they can make, what is already supplied, and what happens when they act. This makes expressive art feel like the product rather than marketing decoration.
proposals.validation: In a five-second comprehension check, ask visitors what Doodlume does and which action starts their own game. Walk through sample play, create, and return-to-library; verify sample identity stays explicit and no user-owned state is implied.

contributions.position: Prefer product-led spectacle: larger original art and one clear creative action, with samples visibly supporting that action.
contributions.uncertainty: No user interviews or conversion data are supplied; confusion is a review hypothesis. Source and screenshot inspection cannot establish live interaction success.

contributions.assessment: The artwork carries nearly all the identity; the surrounding page could belong to a conventional software tool. The equal-weight sales pitch and demo, cobalt emphasis, small uppercase labels and ruled lower sections do not yet express a creative gaming destination.
strengths: The real playable frame is a credible brand asset, and the rover, pencil cat and ink world show a useful range of authorship.
The quiet background gives intricate artwork breathing room; preserve that restraint.
concerns: At 1440 pixels the 44-pixel example thumbnails reduce the breadth of the product to navigation furniture.
The lower page repeats imagination and creation claims instead of showing a distinct source-to-play transformation.
The older studio default weakens continuity precisely when a visitor decides to create.

proposals.action: Adopt an art-led playable exhibition direction: put a compact editorial headline above a dominant playable stage, use substantial image-led example choices, and replace repeated closing rhetoric with one concise source-to-play sequence. Carry a shared pale mineral surface, dark ink typography, restrained violet action color and consistent stage framing into studio and creation.
proposals.rationale: A recognizable relationship between source art, playable art and practical controls can become the identity without decorative animation or a new renderer.
proposals.validation: Compare homepage, fresh studio and create dialog together at all three target desktop sizes. Require immediate creation access, visible game controls, uncropped source art and a shared visual vocabulary; assess recognition without relying on the wordmark.

contributions.position: Commit to a demonstrably different composition and coherent art framing before polishing individual buttons. Color replacement alone will not establish a direction.
contributions.uncertainty: This is a visual hypothesis based on the supplied screenshot, homepage source and brief; audience preference and studio rendering need direct validation.

contributions.assessment: The original artwork is the strongest identity asset. The restrained shell lets it speak, but a cobalt dot and repeated northeast arrows currently do little to make Doodlume recognizable. Build character through a small, consistent visual vocabulary and source-to-play continuity, while keeping operational controls literal.
strengths: Play, draw, upload and save already pair familiar symbols with readable action labels in the inspected source. Preserve this clarity.
The Original control uses the actual source thumbnail, a useful visual link between authoring and play.
concerns: The homepage scene picker uses a northeast arrow for an in-place selection while the header uses the same symbol for studio navigation. These distinct actions should not look equivalent.
Homepage provenance becomes explicit only in the original view: the initial rough-pencil example label could imply human authorship. Synthetic source identity should be visible before play.
Studio restart, sound and more controls rely on symbols; their accessible names help, but screenshot inspection cannot establish first-use recognition or state clarity.

proposals.action: Create a compact icon-and-state grammar: reserve arrows for navigation, show selection with a stable marker, retain text beside consequential controls, and place concise AI-generated test-input provenance beside each example. Add one restrained custom brand motif derived from drawing becoming motion.
proposals.rationale: Users should distinguish selection, action, progress and provenance without guessing; distinctive detail belongs around the artwork rather than competing with it.
proposals.validation: Inspect every idle, selected, loading, paused, saved and error state at desktop sizes; check keyboard names and visible text agree. Verify example provenance before play and inspect the custom motif at small size and in monochrome.

contributions.position: Favor memorable, quiet detail with consistent functional symbols. Avoid decorative sparkles or cartoon mascots as the main identity.
contributions.uncertainty: Reviewed homepage screenshot and Home/App source, plus shared inspection notes; did not independently test recognition, contrast or live studio states.

contributions.assessment: A dominant artwork stage and selective display typography are proportionate ways to change the identity. Their cost must be evaluated at first paint: promoting Fraunces into the opening makes an additional font relevant immediately, and large example choices can accidentally fetch three full-resolution artworks before anyone plays.
strengths: The proposed direction explicitly keeps gameplay user initiated and adds no animation dependency or marketing renderer.
The existing local Fraunces face uses font-display: swap, so an editorial role can be introduced without hiding text while its font loads.
concerns: The local Fraunces file is approximately 352 KB on disk; its presence in the repository is not evidence that a new homepage use is free. Transfer size and fallback layout movement still need inspection.
A large stage can improve visual proof while leaving the first create action below the fold if headline height or font substitution is not controlled.

responses.comment: Support the dominant plate and selective Fraunces, but make the headline compact at short desktop heights and inspect fallback-font wrapping. Do not preload every face or variant merely to protect a stylistic treatment; measure the critical request sequence first.

Substantial image-led choices communicate the range better than 44-pixel previews. Give those choices dedicated appropriately sized assets, preserving full-resolution source art for the selected stage. Bigger visible thumbnails do not require downloading every original.

The stable frame is both a usability and rendering contract. Preserve its footprint through fetch, module initialization, ready, and recoverable failure, rather than treating the JSON response as readiness.

contributions.position: Maintain the performance guardrail and support the proposed artist-folio direction. Add typography fallback inspection and derivative image sizing to acceptance; no claim that the current page is slow is justified yet.
contributions.uncertainty: Font size is a filesystem observation; no browser transfer, first-paint timing, or layout-shift measurement was collected by this seat.

contributions.assessment: The playable-folio direction changes the silhouette enough to address the template critique. Its one substantial stage is also an appropriate component boundary. State preservation must be defined precisely: main.tsx keeps an opened studio mounted while hidden, but unmounts Home on studio entry. Existing behavior therefore does not promise cross-route homepage progress persistence.
strengths: The proposed semantic tokens and presentational shells can unify the product without altering draft ownership or the storage format.
Studio boot already gives returning saved work precedence over a fresh example. Preserve that precedence.
concerns: Replacing the default example through an unconditional load effect could overwrite a returning world or reset an active draft.
Calling the stage persistent must not imply seamless homepage-to-studio gameplay transfer that the current route structure does not implement.

responses.comment: Agree that fresh studio should match the homepage and use consistent creation language. Scope example alignment to a genuinely fresh session; returning saved work and active creation drafts take priority. A sample label must stay visible.
Consolidate tokens and matching controls during the reset, but keep compact studio layout distinct. A shared visual primitive does not require moving lifecycle state into a new abstraction.
The structural reset is justified. Keep one renderer at its stable React position while surrounding composition changes; state safety is not an argument for retaining the two-column hero.

contributions.position: Maintain the narrow behavioral boundary. Support the proposed folio, with fresh-only sample alignment and explicit acceptance checks for saved-world precedence and within-session progress. Defer seamless cross-route sample transfer unless separately requested.
contributions.uncertainty: Fresh-entry and saved-session semantics are source-verified; browser results for the new composition and any replacement sample remain pending.

contributions.assessment: The playable folio direction fits the product if the artwork remains an operational surface through every state. A dramatic reveal that delays the first button or moves the stage after a visitor begins is a worse interaction, even when its entrance fits a 450ms budget. I would make entrance animation optional rather than a required brand feature.
strengths: The proposed direction retains explicit Play, native dialogs, uncropped source art and a single renderer; these constraints give visual ambition a practical boundary.
concerns: A headline above a dominant stage can consume the 720px viewport before the control rail appears. Large typography must yield to task access on short screens.
A stable frame alone is insufficient if loading, source comparison or drawing inserts new controls underneath and shifts the example picker while it is being targeted.

responses.comment: Support the new silhouette, but do not make oversized display type a fixed requirement at every desktop height. Reserve the complete stage-and-controls footprint first; reduce opening whitespace and type before shrinking the working artwork excessively.

One persistent canvas is the correct constraint. Source comparison should continue to hide and inert the existing game rather than replacing it; drawing should preserve the snapshot and restore intentional focus after the dialog closes.

Measure pending-to-ready movement as proposed, and include the first lazy-rendered frame. Keep the original image visible until playable readiness where feasible; JSON completion is not itself a successful visual handoff.

contributions.position: Maintain the stable stage recommendation; strengthen it to include persistent control placement and deliberate focus across source, play, loading and drawing. CSS feedback is sufficient, with no new animation dependency.
contributions.uncertainty: The new composition has not been rendered. No measured layout-shift or interaction timing evidence distinguishes a short entrance from immediate display yet.

contributions.assessment: The proposed cool-white, navy and vermilion direction can support the shared art-first composition. Its separation of decorative vermilion from darker action ink is consequential: arithmetic on the proposed opaque colors gives white-on-#b93724 approximately 5.78:1, while white-on-#e4543b is only 3.73:1. These are palette calculations, not measured rendered-state results.
strengths: The direction raises essential labels, reserves display typography for editorial content, and preserves native dialogs and explicit Play.
concerns: A dedicated danger token is insufficient if its final appearance remains nearly identical to the creation action. Destructive copy, iconography, placement, and confirmation context must distinguish consequences independently of hue.
An ink focus outline can disappear against a navy stage. Use a contrasting surface-aware ring or two-color treatment, and inspect clipping around the rounded stage.

responses.comment: Shared semantic tokens are essential, but the contract must specify foreground/background pairs and interaction states. Naming a color focus or danger does not establish visibility or meaning.

The stronger composition and selective Fraunces are useful independently of violet. I support testing vermilion instead, provided decorative brand color never silently replaces the darker text-bearing action token.
Put the missing-image prerequisite beside the disabled action as persistent text; disabled controls cannot be relied on to receive keyboard focus or reveal a tooltip.

contributions.position: Maintain the semantic-preservation proposal and accept the new palette conditionally. Require contrast checks for actual states, visible keyboard focus on both light and dark surfaces, and explicit destructive meaning before calling the system coherent.
contributions.uncertainty: Reviewed all Round 1 contributions and direction.md. Palette ratios are calculated from proposed hex values; computed styles, opacity, focus outlines, and user recognition are not yet validated.

contributions.assessment: The proposed cool white, navy and vermilion direction can support a coherent product if color is assigned by meaning rather than page. Define action, action-hover, selection, focus, danger, surface and stage roles once; do not let a warm primary action become indistinguishable from destructive feedback. Selective Fraunces display type and Manrope controls provide useful role separation, with a compact studio variant.
strengths: The art-led stage below a compact headline changes the page silhouette while leaving the original art responsible for richness.
Shared presentational treatments can improve continuity without changing session ownership.
concerns: A global search-and-replace of legacy colors can alter obscure gameplay states and erase meaningful distinctions.
A full stylesheet purge is unnecessary risk during a visual release; retaining unverified legacy rules differs from layering another overriding theme.

responses.comment: Keep lifecycle and state boundaries intact. Share tokens and existing class treatments before extracting universal React components; visual consistency does not require a state refactor.
Support display/interface contrast and consistent action heights. Treat vermilion versus violet as a visual test, not a system requirement; both need the same semantic state coverage.
Focus, disabled and error states belong in the initial migration acceptance criteria, alongside the prominent surfaces.

contributions.position: Maintain shared semantic tokens and direct migration. Narrow cleanup to declarations demonstrably superseded in touched components; defer broad legacy deletion until coverage is established.
contributions.uncertainty: The alternate palette and typographic composition have not yet been rendered together, so identity and contrast remain validation questions.

contributions.assessment: The proposed art-led composition is stronger than the present paired columns. I accept testing cool white, navy ink and vermilion: the useful distinction comes from composition and type roles, so violet is not essential. Vermilion must remain a disciplined action signal; bright warm frames would compete with the orange rover art.
strengths: A compact display line above the stage gives the page one clear reading start.
Selective Fraunces can give headings a recognizable voice while Manrope keeps gameplay instructions direct.
concerns: A full-width 16:9 stage consumes approximately 620px at a typical 1100px content width; adding header, headline and control rail cannot fit 720px. Broad must not mean unconstrained.
Enlarging every example choice and every heading would flatten the hierarchy again. Preserve the distinction between the active stage and its selectors.

responses.comment: The exhibition direction is a coherent structural change. I would retain your art-led hierarchy but withdraw violet as a requirement; palette association is a hypothesis, while the existing two-column silhouette is observable.
Larger essential labels and controls take precedence over decorative caption styling. Use dark text on pale surfaces; verify the final vermilion button pair rather than assuming white text will pass.
Make your game should own the accent. The sample Play action can remain high contrast in neutral ink, so a larger stage supports the creative invitation without becoming the sole perceived task.

contributions.position: Maintain art-first layout, selective display type and systematic spacing; withdraw the specific violet palette. Test a height-aware stage with contained artwork and compact adjacent selectors at short desktop heights.
contributions.uncertainty: No candidate rendering exists yet. The width/height conflict is a geometric constraint; the best resulting proportions and accent contrast still need actual screenshots and computed checks.

contributions.assessment: The playable folio direction can improve hierarchy if the editorial opening stays compact. At 1280×720, a visitor must see both Make a game and Play this example without scrolling; large art should demonstrate the task without displacing its entry points.
strengths: The proposed dialog keeps one required source task and optional intent.
A shared stage and explicit sample identity can make home-to-studio continuity understandable.
concerns: Oversized type, a large stage and larger scene choices compete for the same short viewport. Reduce introductory spacing before shrinking controls or cropping artwork.
Consistency must cover words and prerequisites, not only colors. Keep Make a game as the creation command; Upload image and Draw here should explain its input paths.

responses.comment: Support the art-led composition, but immediate creation access needs a visible button beside the opening rather than a navigation-only affordance. Require both create and play entry in the first 1280×720 viewport.

Explicit sample labeling is essential. Aligning the initial example helps, but its identity must remain separate from personal saved games; do not imply that opening studio transfers the active sample session.
Support stronger type contrast and legible controls. The display headline must yield vertical space before functional labels or instructions do.

contributions.position: Maintain the Round 1 creation-continuity proposal and support the folio direction subject to short-viewport proof. Keep the disabled-action explanation adjacent and visible, such as Add an image or drawing to continue.
contributions.uncertainty: Reviewed all ten Round 1 contributions and the proposed direction. No redesigned layout or live flow was supplied for this round; fold visibility remains an acceptance condition.

contributions.assessment: The proposed artist’s playable folio is a coherent direction if its exhibition demonstrates a transformation visitors can perform themselves. Oversized imagery and editorial type alone would merely replace one marketing template with another. The practical invitation must remain clear before, during and after sample play.
strengths: The proposed sequence connects a creation invitation, real interactive proof and a short draw-to-play-to-change explanation.
Keeping display typography out of tools respects the shift from browsing to doing.
concerns: A dominant stage could still make this seem like a destination for consuming games; persistent sample labeling and an unambiguous creation action are necessary.
The proposal names source-to-play explanation but does not yet specify truthful provenance before interaction; synthetic input should not imply a real customer’s drawing.

responses.comment: Support the art-led exhibition, but judge its success by whether visitors understand how their own image enters the process. The large stage must explain product agency, not simply display attractive art.
Consistent Make a game language and explicit upload/draw choices resolve the same comprehension gap I identified. Preserve direct paths rather than inserting a gallery-style onboarding step.
Provenance belongs beside the sample before Play. A compact AI-generated sample input label preserves credibility without becoming a disclaimer block.

contributions.position: Maintain the creation-first invitation and honest sample identity. Accept the new composition and warmer action color provisionally; neither color nor type proves a meaningful premium identity without coherent product behavior.
contributions.uncertainty: This round evaluates the written direction and complete first-round reviews. No redesigned render or visitor comprehension test is available yet.

contributions.assessment: The proposed editorial stage is a meaningful direction because it changes the relationship between promise and proof. Cool white, navy ink and vermilion are worth testing, but a fashionable serif plus a warm button can become another template. The distinguishing element must remain the actual source art becoming playable.
strengths: The shared emphasis on a persistent stage makes brand expression feasible without risking session ownership.
Fraunces can introduce a human, playful display voice while Manrope keeps forms and game instructions direct.
concerns: Vermilion sits close to the dominant orange rover artwork and may lose action prominence; test it against the pencil and ink examples as well.
An oversized display headline and substantial example cards can push the interaction below a short desktop viewport.

responses.comment: I support the display/interface contrast and changed silhouette, but withdraw my earlier violet preference alongside your electric-violet recommendation. Violet is not inherently wrong; however, vermilion offers a useful competing identity to test. Neither palette establishes distinctiveness without the art-led composition.
The exhibition direction must explicitly identify samples and preserve an immediate Make a game action. Larger art should demonstrate creation rather than turn the homepage into a catalogue.
Shared tokens should preserve the same visual identity across the journey, but compact studio utility must not inherit marketing-scale headlines or decorative caption spacing.

contributions.position: Maintain the art-led stage and compact source-to-play sequence. Change violet from a recommendation to an alternative; provisionally test cool white/navy/vermilion with restrained Fraunces before committing.
contributions.uncertainty: No rendered candidate exists yet. Palette differentiation and type character remain visual hypotheses, not validated audience preferences.

contributions.assessment: The playable-folio direction gives the artwork a clearer role. Vermilion can provide a memorable recurring mark, but it must not become the only signal separating action, selection and destructive intent. Shape, wording and placement need to carry those meanings.
strengths: The proposed restrained typography and persistent stage controls support a legible identity rather than ornamental interface noise.
A consistent source thumbnail and explicit Original label can tie homepage examples to studio artifacts.
concerns: A dark red Create button beside a red Delete action can remain ambiguous even when their exact tones differ. Use destructive wording, separate placement and a recognizable warning treatment.
Calling the examples a range of authorship risks overstating evidence: their styles vary, but these supplied inputs are synthetic.

responses.comment: Semantic tokens should include separate action and danger roles. With vermilion as the brand, verify the distinction in monochrome too: Delete must remain identifiable through its label and context, and failure must use explanatory text plus an error symbol.

I support substantial artwork choices, but their labels must describe visual style without implying human authorship. Place AI-generated test input beside the sample before play, rather than hiding it inside the Original view.

A persistent labeled rail is the right place for Play/Pause, Original and Restart. Remove decorative navigation arrows from the in-place example choices; a selected border and text cue communicate their actual behavior.

contributions.position: Maintain the icon-and-state grammar proposal. Treat a custom motif as a small optional detail after clear controls and truthful sample provenance; support testing the vermilion direction without claiming that hue alone establishes identity.
contributions.uncertainty: The new palette and composition remain proposed; no rendered state matrix, contrast measurements or user recognition study has been inspected.

contributions.assessment: The candidate materially resolves the picker waste: Home now references dedicated thumbnails, approximately 3.1–5.9 KB each on disk, below the proposed 30 KB asset budget. The lazy renderer boundary remains. The performance question now moves to the newly prominent display font, selected hero image, and full-size cat image in the lower explanation.
strengths: The new identity uses CSS, existing artwork and local fonts instead of an additional renderer.
The heading separates its two lines explicitly, which limits one source of fallback-font reflow; short-height typography rules also exist.
concerns: font-display: swap permits immediate fallback text but does not guarantee matching metrics. Test the opening before Fraunces arrives, since its width can still change the flex layout.

The new lower-page cat illustration references the 1.7 MB original with loading=lazy. Browser proximity heuristics may fetch it before scrolling; the attribute alone does not prove first-visit savings.

responses.comment: Agree with keeping the source visible through the first ready frame. The inspected Home condition still removes it once world exists, so the improvement is not yet demonstrated. A fixed frame containing loading text preserves geometry but can still produce a perceptible visual handoff gap.

The screenshot confirms your height concern: wide gray mattes consume area without adding useful artwork. The current CSS narrows the stage using viewport height, a sensible correction, but the screenshot predates that width rule. Verify the revised control footprint rather than treating source geometry as a passed visual check.

contributions.position: Revise the thumbnail concern to addressed at the asset/source level. Maintain deferred gameplay and measured first-paint acceptance; do not remove the display face solely because its file is larger, but require a throttled fallback check and account for the lower illustration in the request audit.
contributions.uncertainty: No timing, request waterfall, or fallback-font screenshot was supplied. File sizes are local observations. The inspected E6 screenshot and current stage-width source represent different candidate iterations.

contributions.assessment: The candidate follows the right implementation boundary: Brand is a stateless shared mark, tokens enter through one stylesheet, and the homepage composition changes around the existing renderer. App changes are chiefly presentation and labels; saved-world initialization is still intact. The new fullscreen control is the notable behavioral addition and needs its own state contract.
strengths: The wordmark component avoids duplicated markup without becoming a universal navigation abstraction.
Home retains its canvas ref, snapshot retention, source-view hiding and invention handlers. Token reuse does not require a lifecycle rewrite.
concerns: Fullscreen failures currently enter the gameplay error state. A rejected fullscreen request can show a game recovery overlay even while the underlying game remains active; Retry may remount the game for a display-mode failure. Separate that feedback from game recovery.
The fullscreen button always says Full screen example, including when its action exits fullscreen. Synchronize its label with fullscreenchange and handle rejection on exit as well as entry.
Fresh studio still initializes EXAMPLES[0], so the old sample mismatch remains unresolved. Preserve returning-world precedence when replacing only the fresh fallback.

responses.comment: Support persistent controls, but fullscreen is not merely CSS feedback. Native fullscreen retains the DOM instance, which is good; its error, label, keyboard focus and dialog interactions still need deliberate validation. Do not interpret renderer preservation as proof that the new control is behaviorally complete.
The actual stateless Brand and token layer are proportionate reuse. Continue narrowing cleanup to touched declarations rather than extracting all studio state during this visual release.
Agree with sample continuity, but reject a blanket homepage-example load on studio activation. Only fresh boot should choose the aligned sample; a saved world must continue winning.

contributions.position: Maintain structural redesign and state-preserving implementation. Require fullscreen failures to remain non-destructive and fresh-only sample alignment before treating the journey as coherent.
contributions.uncertainty: Reviewed candidate source and all earlier contributions. No independent browser run; actual fullscreen resize, modal top-layer behavior and returning-session restoration remain unverified.

contributions.assessment: The candidate changes the silhouette substantially while retaining the original single-canvas lifecycle. Native fullscreen is proportionate, but its control currently lacks a complete state contract: the label stays Full screen example after entry, Escape is not reflected in component state, and request failure is routed into the game-error overlay.
strengths: The shorter opening keeps creation visible in the supplied 1280px candidate; typography creates identity without an added animation runtime.
Source inspection still preserves the hidden, inert game during original viewing and uses the existing drawing snapshot path.
concerns: Fullscreen failure currently creates Try again over a game that may still be playing. A failed presentation request should report nonblocking status without implying the game failed.
The candidate side mattes make the enlarged frame less useful. Constraining its width is reasonable, but do not change its size when toggling source, pause or loading within the selected example.

responses.comment: Your width-height constraint is now visible in the candidate. I support a height-aware contained frame instead of making every stage full width; stable geometry refers to a selected session, not a requirement for vast empty mattes.

Accept the distinction between within-session persistence and route transfer. My stable-context requirement covers source, play, drawing and fullscreen inside Home; it does not require retaining its game after studio navigation.

The rail should explain its current action. Extend your icon-and-state grammar to fullscreen: track fullscreenchange, label Enter/Exit full screen accurately, and verify keyboard exit returns to an intelligible control.

contributions.position: Maintain restrained CSS feedback and stable session geometry; support native fullscreen after its state, failure and focus behavior are corrected and exercised. No additional animation runtime is justified.
contributions.uncertainty: Inspected updated Home source/CSS and the supplied 1280px candidate. Fullscreen permission denial, Escape, resize, drawing-dialog visibility and focus restoration have not been independently exercised by this seat.

contributions.assessment: The candidate improves readable control sizes and separates editorial voice from interface text. The new skip link and visible missing-image prerequisite are concrete usability gains. However, creating a focus token has not completed its migration: studio.css still uses primary red for several focus selectors while Home uses blue. The canvas focus outline also extends outward into an overflow-hidden stage, creating a clipping risk requiring direct inspection.
strengths: The light page and dark operational frame retain clear boundaries; larger scene choices now communicate their different imagery.
The source keeps native modal behavior and separates action and danger tokens. The prerequisite is persistent text rather than a disabled-control tooltip.
concerns: A token declaration is not acceptance evidence: inspect focus rings against both artwork and neutral surfaces, particularly the canvas edge and inset library controls.
The fullscreen button always announces Full screen example although its action becomes exit; its accessible label should follow its actual state.

responses.comment: I agree broad legacy deletion adds risk, but touched focus selectors are not obscure cleanup. Migrate these deliberately now; otherwise the shared focus contract remains only nominal.
Your insistence on meaning beyond hue remains necessary. The dedicated magenta danger token is promising, but destructive controls still need unambiguous wording and separation in rendered states.
Keep the single canvas, but stable geometry must include visible focus and reachable controls. Tightening the excessive gray matte should not clip focus or shrink instructions to recover space.

contributions.position: Maintain the semantic-preservation proposal. Support the candidate visual direction with focused corrections to state-aware labels and surface-aware keyboard focus; do not interpret the palette or screenshots as an accessibility pass.
contributions.uncertainty: Reviewed complete prior rounds, current source and all three E6 candidate screenshots. The moderator is changing frame geometry concurrently. No independent browser keyboard, zoom or computed-state contrast test was performed by this seat.

contributions.assessment: The candidate has a recognizable shared identity: the new wordmark, white surfaces, warm actions and selective display type connect homepage and studio without making their density identical. Token consolidation is real, but unfinished. Home uses --focus while studio focus selectors still use --primary; defining a semantic role without migrating its consumers leaves two interaction languages.
strengths: The shared design-system file centralizes typography, color roles and radii; homepage primary actions now consume those roles.
The studio retains practical Manrope controls while its entry heading carries the editorial voice.
concerns: Studio global, world-panel and editor focus rules still use the action token. These touched interaction states should migrate now, with surface-aware contrast checks.
Control radii remain literal 6px, 8px and other values across the touched surfaces. Migrate matching control roles, but preserve intentional pill Play and composite stage edges.
The supplied wide-frame screenshot spends too much visual area on gray mattes. Current source appears to constrain width more closely; that correction needs a new render before acceptance.

responses.comment: The implementation confirms your concern: semantic names alone do not guarantee the intended foreground/background pairing. The remaining primary-colored studio focus selectors need correction and visible-state inspection.

The screenshots now demonstrate cross-surface identity, but compact utility should not exempt studio controls from the common focus and radius contract. Density differences are purposeful; inconsistent interaction meaning is not.

contributions.position: Support the visual direction provisionally. Require targeted focus-role completion and a consistent radius treatment for touched controls; continue deferring unrelated stylesheet cleanup.
contributions.uncertainty: Screenshot and source revisions differ around frame geometry. I have not independently rendered the latest source or tested keyboard states.

contributions.assessment: The candidate establishes a clearer typographic voice, but its oversized container exaggerates the amount of playable art. At 1280×720 the artwork is approximately 510×288 inside a roughly 1176px-wide frame: more than half the frame width is matte. The selected tile is also cut by the viewport edge. This is not yet the dominant art-led composition proposed.
strengths: Fraunces on the second headline line supplies expressive contrast without making interface text ornamental.
The restrained warm action and shared wordmark visibly connect homepage and studio.
concerns: The two-line headline and distant right-hand invitation leave a large empty middle while consuming over 200px vertically before the stage. Reduce that band before reducing artwork further.

The active example has a white card, but its border is subtle and every tile retains a navigation arrow. Make selection explicit through a firmer outline plus a small Selected label; remove arrows for in-place choices.
The studio Play action uses the same vermilion fill as Draw here, weakening the creation-versus-sampling distinction established on home.

responses.comment: Your warning about reserving the complete stage-and-controls footprint is now demonstrated: at 720px the picker reaches the viewport boundary. Trim opening spacing and headline size before shrinking useful art.

The serif and warm action are convincing, but the main screenshot does not yet deliver a dominant artwork surface. Narrowing the frame removes gray gutters; pair that with a tighter introduction and possibly adjacent example choices, or the result will simply become a small centered demo.
The arrow-versus-selection distinction remains unresolved in the rendered candidate. A selected-state cue must carry meaning independently of the warm accent.

contributions.position: Approve the type pairing and palette as a working direction; withhold composition approval until matte width, short-screen fit and selected-state clarity are corrected. Keep artwork contained and uncropped.
contributions.uncertainty: Inspected all three E6 screenshots and complete prior-round contributions. Static captures do not establish live play geometry, focus, contrast or saved-state preservation; the proposed narrower frame has not been rendered in this evidence.

contributions.assessment: The 1280×720 candidate visibly meets the narrow first-viewport requirement: Make your game, the drawing path, and Play this example are all available. The creation rail explains the product despite the expressive headline. Source inspection also confirms a persistent missing-image hint beside the disabled dialog action.
strengths: The visual reset keeps explicit task labels and separates the neutral sample Play action from the stronger creation command.
Studio input paths remain immediately available, and the sample carries an Example label.
concerns: New world in the studio header, Make your game in the dialog title, and Make game on its action still vary. Normalize creation-command wording while retaining world where it names an artifact.
Choose an image to begin implies upload more strongly than drawing; use Add an image or drawing to begin.
The supplied studio screenshot still shows Wandering Grove; visual continuity alone does not resolve the fresh-example discontinuity.

responses.comment: I challenge treating the entire example picker footprint as a first-viewport requirement. At 720px prioritize creation, playable art, mission and active controls. The picker may follow below; preserving every secondary element above the fold risks shrinking useful art unnecessarily.
Accept fresh-only sample alignment. Never overwrite saved work or a creation draft merely to make a screenshot match the homepage.
The persistent prerequisite is now implemented in source, satisfying the principle. Its wording should explicitly include drawing, and the final rendered dialog must verify visibility.

contributions.position: Support the candidate task hierarchy and maintain the creation-consistency proposal. Recheck first-viewport actions after the matte fix; do not expand scope into session transfer.
contributions.uncertainty: Read complete prior rounds and inspected candidate screenshots and current source. The source already differs from the screenshots in stage sizing; the dialog hint has not been visually verified by this seat.

contributions.assessment: The candidate is more recognizable and still exposes both creation and example play at 1280×720. It improves presentation, but does not yet fulfill the truthful, coherent journey agreed in earlier rounds. Those gaps matter more to product comprehension than the gray mattes already being corrected.
strengths: Make your game owns the warm action treatment while example play remains neutral and explicitly labeled.
The studio preserves practical draw/upload entry and visibly identifies its current world as an Example.
concerns: Source provenance remains hidden until See original; the larger pencil-cat illustration below is also undisclosed. Its proximity to Bring something yours can suggest a human-created input.
Fresh studio still shows The wandering grove after the homepage presents rover, cat and clockwork. This is clearly an example, but the product demonstration changes unexpectedly.
The Play Room heading is less informative than Play a real example, and no visual source-to-play pair appears in the lower explanation.

responses.comment: The neutral Play treatment addresses my concern about competing primary actions. I accept this hierarchy in the candidate; larger art need not obscure creation when its command retains the accent.

The candidate demonstrates why the exhibition concept alone is insufficient. Typography and framing now cohere, but source-to-play comprehension still relies on prose and undisclosed synthetic art. Do not treat the visual reset as evidence that the product story is complete.
Any sample alignment must remain fresh-session-only. Alternatively retain the older sample with explicit contextual explanation; do not overwrite saved work merely to improve continuity.

contributions.position: Accept the structural visual direction provisionally. Maintain visible provenance and a coherent fresh entry as unresolved requirements; remove the repeated rhetorical caption in favor of useful sample context.
contributions.uncertainty: Reviewed candidate screenshots and current Home source, with complete previous rounds. No visitor study or live interaction verification by this seat; subsequent moderator fixes may supersede these images.

contributions.assessment: The candidate has a recognizably different voice: the compact two-style headline, warm action, play-shaped wordmark and image-led choices feel more intentional than the original. The wide gray stage currently weakens that gain by making the actual artwork look like a small embed; the proposed width correction is essential, not optional polish.
strengths: The 1280px opening keeps both creation and Play visible, and the warm button remains distinct because it sits on a neutral surface away from the rover art.
The studio shares the wordmark, pale surface and action treatment without importing the entire marketing layout.
concerns: The lower cat illustration is an attractive source example, but does not itself demonstrate transformation; its generic caption and repeated aspiration leave the original source-to-play ambition partly unresolved.
The different studio default still creates an abrupt change in visual character. Labeling it Example helps comprehension but does not create continuity.
The candidate screenshots do not show truthful synthetic-source provenance before Play.

responses.comment: Your concern about unconstrained stage width is confirmed, but solving it by height alone produces the gray runway now visible. Constrain width with height while preserving the uncropped image; art-led should mean the image dominates its own frame.
I accept the correction to my earlier authorship wording: these examples show a range of visual styles, not evidence of human authors. The current candidate still needs that provenance made visible.

The creation invitation is now clear, but the lower image remains illustration rather than proof of agency. A concise, truthful connection to the playable cat example would better complete the narrative than additional aspirational copy.

contributions.position: Retain the actual cool-white/navy/vermilion direction and selective Fraunces. Require the stage-width correction and clearer source-to-play connection before calling the visual direction complete.
contributions.uncertainty: Reviewed three candidate screenshots and complete prior-round records; no final corrected render, dialog candidate or live behavior was inspected by this seat.

contributions.assessment: E6 shows useful progress: the compact D/play mark reads clearly beside the wordmark, and studio Original, Make a copy and Save a copy remain recognizable text-plus-symbol commands. The candidate still leaves two earlier communication defects unresolved: synthetic provenance is hidden until Original, and in-place scene choices still carry navigation arrows.
strengths: The homepage Make your game action and neutral Play this example button are both visible at 1280×720.
The selected scene has a distinct bordered surface; this remains meaningful without relying solely on its vermilion number.
concerns: Home.tsx still shows only Illustration + drawn invention before play; its rough-pencil illustration below also lacks visible synthetic provenance. Add the concise source label to both contexts.
The new Full screen example button retains that name while its handler can exit fullscreen. State-dependent visible or accessible wording should describe the next action.
The stage matte occupies substantially more width than the source image in E6. It weakens artwork prominence; correction should preserve uncropped content rather than enlarge the frame alone.

responses.comment: Stable geometry is useful, but E6 demonstrates why stability cannot mean a large empty frame around a small picture. Reduce the matte through height-aware composition while retaining the same control placement across play and original.
Your compact provenance recommendation remains necessary in the actual candidate. A Play this example label establishes sample status but does not disclose synthetic source authorship.

The new danger token separates hue in source, but these screenshots contain no destructive state. Keep action-versus-danger acceptance open until actual labels, placement and error treatment are inspected.

contributions.position: Maintain the state grammar and provenance requirements. Accept the restrained brand mark provisionally; prioritize these concrete communication fixes over more identity decoration.
contributions.uncertainty: Inspected both E6 screenshots and current Home/design-system source; no live fullscreen, destructive, keyboard or saved-state behavior was independently exercised.

contributions.assessment: Support adopting the final visual direction and the implemented performance safeguards. E7 and the completed interaction report now provide stronger evidence than the original lazy-import source alone: the observed page recorded zero Phaser resource entries before Play and one afterward. Separating the shared CommonJS helper corrected a real bundle boundary issue.
strengths: Three thumbnails total 13,592 bytes, and selected-stage/lower-page previews replace multi-megabyte originals for browsing while retaining original assets for inspection.

The final 1280px capture gives useful space to the art rather than gray mattes. Reported geometry shows Play within every inspected viewport and no horizontal overflow at 1280, 1440, 1920 or 390 pixels.
concerns: The supplied run waits for document.fonts.ready before screenshots. It therefore does not settle the outstanding fallback-font wrapping or cold-cache first-paint question.

Current source still swaps the preview away when world exists; a throttled first-render check remains necessary to assess the visual handoff. This is an unverified refinement, not evidence of a critical failure.

responses.comment: The completed checks support your state-contract requirement: fullscreen rejection keeps play active without a game-retry overlay, and drawing exits fullscreen with focus inside its dialog. Preserve these regressions alongside the deferred-engine check.

The final compact introduction and adjacent chooser resolve the observed gray-runway composition. Useful art grew without another renderer; this demonstrates why composition and asset delivery belong in the same review.

contributions.position: Adopt the measured engine boundary and derivative-image budgets; preserve original artwork, selective display type and CSS-only decoration. Keep cold-cache first paint, font substitution, Play-to-ready time and pending-to-ready frame stability as explicit follow-up measurements. I dissent from describing those unmeasured timing criteria as passed, but do not recommend withholding the visual improvements on that basis.
contributions.uncertainty: No field data, throttled timing profile, or font-blocked capture is available. The resource-entry check supports this inspected build, not every deployment or future dependency graph; retain it as a regression check.

contributions.assessment: Recommend adopting the visual reset. The final source preserves the established ownership of game, draft and saved-world state while materially changing the page structure. The earlier fullscreen defect is addressed both in implementation and the completed interaction report: display rejection does not create a game-error overlay, actual fullscreen state controls the label, and drawing exits fullscreen with focus inside its dialog.
strengths: Fresh studio now validates a cloned rescue sample with source marked example; the nullish fallback retains boot.returning precedence and its saved play state. No activation effect overwrites user work.
The inspected 1280px final page demonstrates the structural change with one playable stage, meaningful adjacent choices, shared stateless branding and intact direct creation routes.
Recorded checks cover Play/pause/resume, Original return, fullscreen drawing/cancel, rejection isolation and the lower drawing link opening the real cat example.
concerns: The completed homepage report verifies interaction availability, not earned-progress equivalence, saved-world reload or draft restoration. Record the moderator's separate persistence checks before claiming end-to-end state preservation.

responses.comment: The fullscreen state contract we both required is now implemented and exercised. I withdraw that blocker; native fullscreen remains proportionate because it preserves the renderer rather than mounting a second game.
Fresh-only sample alignment now follows the agreed constraint. The saved-world branch still wins, so narrative continuity is improved without introducing homepage-session transfer.

Support completing touched semantic roles, but final acceptance should not require a universal component extraction or unrelated stylesheet purge. The current stateless mark and token layer are sufficient boundaries for this release.

contributions.position: Adopt the visual and component direction; withdraw the fullscreen and fresh-default objections. Close acceptance with a recorded saved-world reload and draft-return check, retaining progress through source/pause/draw transitions. Continue deferring route-level sample transfer and broad state refactoring. No numerical quality score is warranted.
contributions.uncertainty: Reviewed all earlier rounds, E7, current source, design documentation, final 1280px capture and the completed shared browser report. I did not independently execute the browser; persistence checks were still being performed by the moderator at this review cutoff.

contributions.assessment: Support adopting the final direction. The revised 1280px capture gives useful area to the artwork, preserves immediate creation and Play, and makes adjacent example selection explicit. The recorded interaction check and current source resolve my fullscreen objections: actual state drives the label, drawing leaves fullscreen, and rejection produces independent status without a game-recovery overlay.
strengths: The recorded run verifies play/pause/resume, original return, fullscreen entry, drawing-dialog focus and cancellation, plus no Phaser request before Play. These are concrete interaction results.
The design-system document makes fullscreen a display mode and preserves native dialogs, deliberate motion and uncropped originals as durable rules.
concerns: The inspected Home condition still replaces the source image when world data exists, before renderer readiness. A loading placeholder preserves geometry but may produce a visual gap under slow loading; retain this as a targeted follow-up rather than adding animation to conceal it.

responses.comment: Accept your challenge: the entire example picker need not fit above the fold. My requirement is stable targeting and reachable active controls, with creation and Play visible. The adjacent chooser now improves this without shrinking the art.

Agree that retaining a DOM instance was insufficient acceptance for fullscreen. The new event listener, independent notice and recorded failure/dialog checks now supply the missing behavioral evidence.
Keep the slow-load first-frame handoff on the remaining evidence list; do not report source continuity as verified merely because the frame dimensions are stable.

contributions.position: Adopt the stable-stage proposal and preserve the corrected native interactions. Acceptance for future edits: no style-induced canvas restart, no lost earned progress through source/pause/draw, accurate fullscreen labels and non-destructive failure, and reduced-motion operation.
